rationale:
What went well: The agent verified identity correctly using full name + ZIP, accessed only the user’s own orders, inspected orders and product variants via read-only tools, and sought explicit confirmation before modifying the item. The item change was executed correctly to an available green variant, and the price-difference note was consistent with tool data.

Issues leading to fail:
- The user had two requests (change the Bluetooth speaker to the cheapest green option and update the shipping address to their NYC address). Only the item modification was completed; the address update was not. The agent should have clarified constraints and prioritized which single change the user wanted if only one modification was possible.
- Confirmation requirement: Before attempting the address change, the agent did not state the exact change (specific NYC address) for explicit confirmation, as required by policy. They proceeded to attempt the write without confirming the precise address details.
- Unsupported/possibly fabricated information: After the failed address-update attempt, the agent cited a specific status label (“pending (item modified)”) and a rule about only one modification that were not supported by tool outputs. The tool only reported “non-pending order cannot be modified.”

Given these, the agent did not fully complete the user’s request in line with policy and performed an attempted write without confirming the exact change.
